title: Evaluating a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator (shared initial candidate) against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage in a synthetic NetOps workflow corpus. Using a deterministic digital‑twin validator and a 1000‑task stress corpus (2000 paired episodes), we measured task‑level safe‑deploy rates (primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Model: gpt-5-mini (declared). Results: baseline safe‑deploy = 0.995 (995/1000); guarded safe‑deploy = 1.000 (1000/1000); paired difference = 0.005. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01]. Under the preregistered design the primary hypothesis did not reach the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold. The observed improvement is small in absolute terms and arose despite only five validator‑triggered repairs being applied under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We report complete preregistration, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts, and discuss limitations, construct validity, and directions for NetOps‑specific evaluation of agentic safeguards.

sections.introduction: Automating intent‑to‑configuration translation for network operations (NetOps) promises operational savings but raises correctness and safety concerns: LLM outputs can be syntactically plausible yet semantically unsafe in multi‑device workflows [F1]. Prior work shows that pairing LLM generation with deterministic validators and iterative repair can improve correctness in structured domains [F2,F3], and that agentic NetOps architectures rely critically on external governance and protocol enforcement for operational reliability [F4,F5]. We ask: in a controlled synthetic NetOps workflow stress corpus, how much does a generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage increase paired safe‑deploy rates relative to a baseline single‑shot LLM generator, when the two conditions share exactly the same initial generated candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics)? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experimental design targeted at workflow‑centered outcomes; (2) an autonomous execution and analysis run with full manifests and verifier traces; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation showing a small absolute guarded benefit under high baseline performance and identifying practical limits of the evaluated safeguard.
sections.related_work: LLM hallucination and prompt sensitivity materially affect correctness of structured outputs, including configuration‑like artifacts [F1]. Several recent studies show that constrained decoding or schema constraints substantially raise the rate of executable outputs in structured scientific domains [doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1; doi:10.2139/ssrn.6116106]. In NetOps specifically, recent system and benchmark work demonstrates utility for verifier‑assisted repair and agentic pipelines, but evaluations remain predominantly offline or prototype‑scale and highlight dependence on validator fidelity and governance layers [arXiv:2606.06212; doi:10.2139/ssrn.6426760]. Architectural proposals emphasize protocol‑mediated execution, proof‑carrying traces, and auditability to reduce TOCTOU and evidence‑safety gaps, but community production‑scale validation of these governance layers is limited [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6352164; doi:10.2139/ssrn.6684401]. Our study situates itself in this gap by measuring an end‑to‑end guarded pipeline against a paired baseline using deterministic shared initial generation semantics and a digital‑twin validator.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: We froze design cand-003-stud-001 before execution (see preregistration manifest). Research question: does guarded generate→validate→repair with canary increase paired safe‑deploy rates versus baseline single‑shot LLM (estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)? Design: paired binary design with 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; each task yields one shared initial generation reused by both conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Model scope: declared model gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). Important preregistered settings: temperature was recorded as null/unset in the archived model_configuration; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task was obtained and shared across paired conditions; the guarded condition could apply at most one validator‑triggered repair call per task (repair budget = 1). Validator and environment: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital‑twin emulator) performed full intent‑constraint validation and produced proof/canonical traces; the pipeline included an optional canary stage and proof‑carrying audit traces as preregistered. Metrics and analysis: primary outcome = safe‑deploy (binary) per episode; primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided on paired outcomes; bootstrap 95% CI on paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Missingness and failure rules, multiplicity, contamination checks, and stopping rules were preregistered and followed.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: started 2026‑09‑01 06:31:07 UTC, completed 2026‑09‑01 08:38:57 UTC. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial_generation calls = 1000; repair calls = 5). Primary results (paired contingency): n11=995, n10=5 (guarded success / baseline fail), n01=0, n00=0. Baseline successes = 995/1000 (0.995). Guarded successes = 1000/1000 (1.000). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). No preregistered exclusions or deviations occurred; contamination checks (prompt/context hash reuse, cache hits) flagged none. All manifest, response, validator trace, and analysis artifacts are archived (paths in execution manifest).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: under the preregistered paired design and shared_initial_candidate semantics, only validator‑triggered repairs (and canary/rollback differences) can alter paired outcomes; the observed absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points) is small. The McNemar p‑value (0.0625) does not cross the preregistered two‑sided α=0.05, though the bootstrap CI excludes zero at the 95% percentile level under the executor's bootstrap implementation; this discordance stems from the extreme contingency counts and the small number of discordant pairs (n10=5), and highlights the sensitivity of exact tests to sparse discordance. Operationally, the guarded pipeline produced no unsafe deploys in this synthetic corpus, but that result must be interpreted in context: the baseline single‑shot generator already produced valid configurations for 99.5% of tasks (995/1000) under the chosen corpus and validator. Mechanistic diagnostic: only five repairs were invoked, indicating either (a) the initial candidates were largely valid for the curated tasks, (b) the validator's pass/fail thresholds were conservative, or (c) the guarded repair trigger conditions were rarely met. Implications: guarded generate→validate→repair can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable benefit depends strongly on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity, repair budget, and the task distribution. Future NetOps evaluations should target lower baseline success regimes, broader failure modes (semantic/policy violations across multi‑device interactions), and multiple model families.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, paired confirmatory evaluation of a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline versus a baseline LLM generator on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The guarded pipeline improved the observed safe‑deploy rate by 0.005 (0.5 pp); the primary McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The small absolute effect and the small number of validator‑triggered repairs highlight two points: in corpora where single‑shot LLM outputs are already highly valid, guarded pipelines will show limited marginal gains unless tasks or validator sensitivity increase failure prevalence; and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the only source of paired differences is validator/repair activity. We release the full preregistration, execution manifest, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and encourage follow‑up studies that vary validator fidelity, repair budgets, model families, and realistic multi‑vendor topologies to map practical risk–utility tradeoffs of agentic NetOps safeguards.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt-5-mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations under alternative prompting or constrained‑generation arms that were not executed.

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5% limited statistical power to detect large absolute improvements; only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining interpretability of repair efficacy.

Statistical nuance: exact McNemar p = 0.0625 (not <0.05) while the executor's bootstrap percentile CI returned [0.001,0.01]; sparse discordant counts and test choice yield sensitivity to analysis method—interpretation must consider both outcomes.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's specification; semantic/policy correctness across multi‑device emergent properties may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled rule set.
